title: The Infinitive
subtitle: Wishing to do, going to do · the -tuṃ ending

revision.title: Quick Revision — Lesson IX
revision.summaryHtml: In Lesson IX you learned the gerund: -tvā (or -ya after a prefix) means “having done”. It is an earlier action by the same person, it never changes its ending, and it comes before the main verb.
revision.connectionHtml: Connection: The gerund looks back (“having gone”). The infinitive looks forward (“to go”): what someone wants or goes in order to do.

questions.q: Does a gerund change when the subject is plural?
questions.a: No, it is indeclinable. Only the main verb changes.

questions.q: Say “Having gone home, the man sleeps.”

blocks.html: The infinitive expresses purpose or wish: “to cook”, “to go”, “in order to eat”. Like the gerund, it is indeclinable: one fixed form, whatever the subject.

blocks.title: Forming the infinitive
formulas: root + (i) + -tuṃ | pac + i + tuṃ = pacituṃ (to cook)

blocks.caption: Common infinitives
head: Verb
Infinitive
Meaning
rows: to see (irregular: learn it as it is)

blocks.html: 1 · A wish. With icchati (wishes), ussahati (tries), ārabhati (begins) or sakkoti (is able), the infinitive says what is wished, tried, begun or possible.
2 · A purpose. With a verb of motion (goes, comes, climbs), the infinitive says why: “goes to eat”.

blocks.title: Pattern: purpose
formulas: Subject + object + infinitive + place + verb of motion

blocks.html: Compare: bhuñjitvā gacchati = “having eaten, he goes” (eating happened first). bhuñjituṃ gacchati = “he goes to eat” (eating is the goal).

items.why: Choose -tuṃ for a goal and -tvā for something already done.
The infinitive stays the same for one or many; only icchati / icchanti changes.
The main verb stands last in the sentence.

examples.english: The man wishes to cook rice.
The child comes home to drink water.
The disciples go to the monastery to ask about the Dhamma.
The washerman goes down to the water to wash the clothes.
The farmer tries to plough the field.

english: The boy wishes to go to the park.
The boy wants to go to the park.
The birds come down from the trees to eat grass.
Birds descend from the trees to eat grass.
The sailor tries to cross the sea.
The uncle begins to cook rice.
The lay devotees go to the monastery to give alms.
Lay devotees go to the monastery to give alms.
The merchant goes to the city to bring goods.
The man wishes to go to the village.
The farmer goes to plough the field.
The boys wish to drink water.
The good man goes to the monastery to ask a question.

exercises.instruction: Translate into English. Spot the infinitive (-tuṃ) first, then decide: wish or purpose?

items.answer: The lay devotee goes to the monastery to ask a question.
alts: A lay devotee goes to the monastery to ask a question.
The lay devotee goes to the monastery to ask the question.

items.answer: The bird comes to the tree to eat a fruit.
alts: The bird comes to the tree to eat the fruit.
The bird comes to the tree to eat fruit.
A bird comes to the tree to eat a fruit.

items.answer: The farmer wishes to dig a pit with a hoe.
alts: The farmer wants to dig a pit with a hoe.
The farmer wishes to dig the pit with a hoe.
A farmer wishes to dig a pit with a hoe.

items.prompt: Nāviko samuddaṃ taritvā dīpaṃ gantuṃ icchati.
items.answer: The sailor, having crossed the sea, wishes to go to the island.
alts: Having crossed the sea, the sailor wishes to go to the island.
The sailor, having crossed the sea, wants to go to the island.

items.prompt: Mātulo puttena saddhiṃ nagaraṃ gantuṃ ussahati.
items.answer: The uncle tries to go to the city with his son.
alts: The uncle tries to go to the city with the son.
The uncle tries to go to the city with a son.

items.answer: The merchants go to the city to bring goods.
alts: Merchants go to the city to bring goods.
The merchants go to the city to fetch goods.

items.answer: The good man begins to give alms.
alts: A good man begins to give alms.
The good man begins to give a gift.
The good man begins to give gifts.

items.answer: The washerman goes down to the water to wash the clothes.
alts: The washerman descends to the water to wash the clothes.
The washerman goes down to the water to wash clothes.
The washerman descends to the water to wash clothes.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Pāli. Use the infinitive and keep the main verb last.

items.prompt: The boy wishes to go to the monastery.
alts: Dārako vihāraṃ gantuṃ icchati.

items.prompt: The farmer goes to the field to plough.
alts: Kassako kasituṃ khettaṃ gacchati.

items.prompt: The man wishes to see the Buddha.
alts: Puriso Buddhaṃ daṭṭhuṃ icchati.
Naro Tathāgataṃ daṭṭhuṃ icchati.
Puriso Tathāgataṃ daṭṭhuṃ icchati.

items.prompt: The merchants wish to drink water.
alts: Vāṇijā udakaṃ pivituṃ icchanti.

items.prompt: The child enters the house to eat rice.
alts: Kumāro bhattaṃ khādituṃ gehaṃ pavisati.
Dārako gehaṃ bhattaṃ khādituṃ pavisati.
